<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ### 角色与背景定义
> 你是资深MySQL内核研发专家，精通MySQL 8.0+代码库结构、版本迭代历史、错误分类体系，熟悉MySQL官方代码仓库（GitHub/Oracle）的提交规范、PR描述格式、Issue标签体系，能够精准识别不同错误的根因、影响模块、修复模式。
> 
> ### 核心任务目标
> 基于下方提供的20类MySQL内核错误/性能问题清单（DEG-001至DEG-020），检索MySQL代码库历史中（包括但不限于提交记录、Pull Request、Issue、官方bug库、修复补丁）的**相似错误**，需完成：
> 1. 对每一类目标错误，匹配至少1-3个历史相似错误；
> 2. 分析相似错误的核心特征（根因、影响模块、表现形式）；
> 3. 给出相似错误的修复方案、关联提交哈希/PR编号。
> 
> ### 错误分类与相似性判定标准
> 先对目标错误（DEG-001至DEG-020）进行分类，再按以下维度检索相似错误：
> | 错误大类                | 包含的DEG编号                | 相似性判定维度                                                                 |
> |-------------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
> | 1. 性能劣化/资源分配问题 | DEG-001、004、013、015       | 影响模块（如查询优化器/存储引擎）、根因（如内存过度分配/CPU高占用/IO优化不当）、表现（QPS下降/延迟升高） |
> | 2. 锁竞争/并发问题       | DEG-007、011、016、017       | 锁类型（全局锁/行锁/表锁）、竞争场景（高并发读写/线程间竞争）、表现（挂起/死锁/吞吐量下降）             |
> | 3. 内存泄漏/资源释放问题 | DEG-006、008、009、010、012、019 | 资源类型（内存/文件句柄/对象池）、泄漏场景（错误路径/析构阶段/批量操作）、根因（未释放/未归还对象）     |
> | 4. 参数配置/行为变更问题 | DEG-003、014                 | 配置参数（back_log/innodb_thread_concurrency）、根因（逻辑移除/返回值处理不当/行为变更）               |
> | 5. 平台兼容性问题        | DEG-005、015                 | 目标平台（Linux/Windows）、根因（动态链接/MMAP/Overlapped使用不当）               |
> | 6. 执行逻辑错误          | DEG-018、020                 | 影响操作（多表更新/对象池管理）、根因（执行顺序错误/对象未归还）                   |
> 
> ### 输入的目标错误清单
> DEG-001	将 Linux 平台捆绑的 ICU 从静态库改为共享库（动态链接），影响正则匹配路径的编译优化
> DEG-002	启动阶段扫描目录并读取每个 .ibd 文件页头以识别 Space ID
> DEG-003	恢复允许 back_log=0，并在初始化时自动将其设为 max_connections（默认仍为 10000）；修复 WL#16888 移除旧逻辑引发的行为变更
> DEG-004	为范围扫描引入动态 Record_buffer 策略（按估算行数的 1/10 分配，最小 4KB，最大 128KB），修复此前过度分配导致的性能回归
> DEG-005	移除 OS_FILE_NORMAL/OS_FILE_AIO 的误导语义，Windows 平台默认使用 Overlapped（FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED）避免内核串行
> DEG-006	异步接口移除非线程安全的静态局部变量，避免跨线程持久化状态导致的内存泄漏
> DEG-007	多个发送线程竞争同一 send_lock
> DEG-008	解析器外部创建的 Item 对象未加入 thd->m_item_list，导致未被释放
> DEG-009	CachedObject::operator= 在赋新对象前未释放旧对象，导致会话泄漏
> DEG-010	批量导入错误路径未释放资源，导致导入失败后内存不下降
> DEG-011	m_node_total_send_buffer_size 更新缺乏一致的锁保护
> DEG-012	datadir 为空时，析构阶段释放临时配置路径字符串，避免内存泄漏
> DEG-013	引入选择性 / 动态 Offload；对 “极快查询（cost<10）” 跳过动态 Offload，避免三阶段优化额外开销
> DEG-014	64 位系统返回值截断（(DWORD)-1）且错误处理不当导致无限重试
> DEG-015	压缩表默认 mmap，超大文件在旧内核中引发换页和高 sys CPU
> DEG-016	当 innodb_thread_concurrency=1 时，内部临时表操作未正确处理并发票导致挂起
> DEG-017	THD::LOCK_query_plan 锁粒度过大或持锁过久
> DEG-018	引擎层未正确处理多表 Update 的执行顺序
> DEG-019	特定错误场景 ALLOC_MEM 未释放
> DEG-020	GCI 操作对象未在所有路径归还对象池
> 
> ### 输出要求（结构化）
> #### 1. 相似错误检索总览
> 列出每个DEG编号对应的相似错误数量、核心相似维度（如“内存泄漏-错误路径未释放资源”）。
> 
> #### 2. 分DEG详细检索结果（每个DEG至少1条相似错误）
> 格式示例：
> ##### DEG-010：批量导入错误路径未释放资源，导致导入失败后内存不下降
> - 相似错误1：
>   - 错误描述：批量导出（SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE）失败时，未释放文件句柄和临时内存缓冲区，导致文件句柄泄漏、内存占用持续升高

author: copilot
body:
Cloud Run container failed to start on PORT=8080 due to the server crashing before it could bind to the port.

### Root Causes

- **Firebase Admin initialization order**: `api.js` was required before `admin.initializeApp()`, but `api.js` calls `admin.firestore()` at module load time, causing immediate crash
- **Express 5 breaking change**: Wildcard routes using `"*"` throw `PathError` in Express 5 / path-to-regexp v8

### Changes

- Move `admin.initializeApp()` before requiring `./controllers/api`
- Update wildcard routes from `"*"` to `"/{*path}"` (Express 5 syntax)

```js
// Before: api.js loaded before Firebase initialized
const apiRouter = require("./controllers/api");
admin.initializeApp();  // Too late - api.js already crashed

// After: Initialize first
admin.initializeApp();
const apiRouter = require("./controllers/api");  // Now safe

// Express 5 wildcard syntax
app.get("/{*path}", (req, res) => { ... });  // was: "*"
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Firebase Cloud Run rollout failure: container failed to start on PORT=8080</issue_title>

> 
> ```
> An error occurred in your rollout
> generic::failed_precondition: The user-provided container failed to start and listen on the port defined provided by the PORT=8080 environment variable within the allocated timeout. This can happen when the container port is misconfigured or if the timeout is too short. The health check timeout can be extended.  Logs for this revision might contain more information. 
> ```

> **Logs:** [View rollout logs in Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/viewer?project=sudoku-labs&resource=cloud_run_revision/service_name/sudoku/revision_name/sudoku-build-2025-12-19-025&advancedFilter=resource.type%3D%22cloud_run_revision%22%0Aresource.labels.service_name%3D%22sudoku%22%0Aresource. labels.revision_name%3D%22sudoku-build-2025-12-19-025%22)
> 
> For more troubleshooting guidance, see [Cloud Run container failed to start](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/troubleshooting#container-failed-to-start).
> 
> **Details:**
> - The app's container failed to start and listen on the expected port (PORT=8080) within the timeout window.
> - Possible causes: misconfigured container port, startup timeout too short, or application not binding to the correct port in the Dockerfile/config. 
> 
> **Action items:**
> - Review container port configuration and ensure the app is listening on PORT=8080.
> - Consider extending the health check timeout for Cloud Run.
> - Consult deployment logs for more details.

## 📌 Summary
Adds human-readable sequential session numbers (#001, #002, #003...) to improve conversation clarity and tracking without relying on database UUIDs.

## 🎯 Changes
- **Database**: Added `session_number` column with PostgreSQL sequence for auto-increment
- **Backend**: Updated `CashSessionRead` schema to include session number
- **Frontend**: Display formatted session numbers (#001 format) in:
  - Dashboard sessions table (merged with date column)
  - Session detail page header
  - Close session form header
  - Edit session forms (open/closed)
- **Migration**: Backfills existing sessions with sequential numbers ordered by date/time

## 🔢 Numbering Strategy
- **Global sequence**: Numbers never reset, continuous across all businesses
- **Auto-increment**: Database sequence handles assignment automatically
- **Format**: Zero-padded 3 digits (#001, #002, etc.) for consistent display
- **No per-business reset**: Simplified approach, avoids complexity

author: eddy-dev0
body:
### Motivation

- Ensure the desktop UI shows a reasonable, timezone-aware market timestamp even when the local price cache is stale.
- Surface that the displayed timestamp is an estimate so users are not misled by stale cached data.
- Reuse the same cache-freshness logic as the pipeline (`CACHE_MAX_AGE`) to keep behaviour consistent between core and UI.

### Description

- Added a cache-freshness helper `._is_cache_timestamp_fresh(...)` to `stock_predictor/ui_app.py` and imported `CACHE_MAX_AGE` from `core.pipeline`.
- Introduced a new flag `self.market_timestamp_live_estimate` on the UI app to mark when the timestamp was derived as a live estimate.
- Updated `_resolve_market_timestamp()` to:
  - Inspect `self.price_history.attrs.get("cache_timestamp")` when `price_history` exists.
  - If the cache is fresh, use the latest price point from `price_history` as before.
  - If the cache is stale, try a lightweight live lookup via the pipeline fetcher (`self.application.pipeline.fetcher.fetch_live_price(force=False)`), fall back to `self._now()` if unavailable, and set `market_timestamp_live_estimate = True`.
  - Update `market_timestamp_stale` to reflect stale cache cases.
- Updated `_update_metrics()` to append `"(live estimate)"` to the `as_of` display and to prefer showing the live-estimate timestamp in the status message instead of the generic stale message.
- Updated tests in `StockPredictor/tests/test_ui_app_market_timestamp.py`:
  - Ensure a fresh cache path is covered by setting `price_history.attrs['cache_timestamp']` in the price-history test.
  - Added `test_market_timestamp_live_estimate_for_stale_cache()` to assert the `"(live estimate)"` suffix and that status includes a live-estimate note.

### Testing

- Ran `pytest -q StockPredictor/tests/test_ui_app_market_timestamp.py`.
- Test result: `4 passed` (all tests in the file succeeded).
- Tests exercise both fresh-cache behaviour and stale-cache live-estimate fallback in the UI layer.

author: candyeeyewear
body: Implement RLS-safe conversation deletion by introducing a `leave_conversation` RPC and updating the client to use it, resolving RLS violations and preventing deleted conversations from reappearing. The original implementation attempted to directly update or delete `conversations` rows from the client, which frequently triggered Supabase Row Level Security (RLS) policies and caused the database write to fail. This PR fixes this by moving the deletion logic into a `SECURITY DEFINER` PostgreSQL function (RPC), which can execute with elevated privileges, thus bypassing client-side RLS restrictions for this specific operation. The client now calls this RPC and only updates its local state upon successful completion. ---

body:
This pull request enhances the release workflow by introducing automated notifications for pull requests included in a release. It adds a new workflow to identify PRs from release notes and post comments and labels on them, making it easier for contributors to track when their work is released. The changes also extend support for multiple PR link formats in release notes and ensure the notification process is configurable.

**Release workflow enhancements:**

* Added a new input parameter `notify-prs` to the `RELEASE.yaml` workflow, allowing optional triggering of PR notifications when a release is published.
* Introduced a new job `notify-prs-released` in `RELEASE.yaml` that runs the `NOTIFY_PRS_RELEASED.yml` workflow to notify PRs, with conditional execution based on release status and the new input parameter.

**PR notification workflow improvements:**

* Updated the PR extraction logic in `NOTIFY_PRS_RELEASED.yml` to support both standard changelog PR links (`(#1234)`) and extended formats (`(PR #1234 by @username)`), ensuring more comprehensive PR detection.
* Enhanced the notification step to not only post comments but also add release-specific labels (e.g., `released/v1.2.3`) to each PR, improving visibility for contributors. # 📋 Summary
This Pull Request introduces full mobile touch control support for players in Cooperative Mode, enhancing usability on handheld devices. This includes mapping standard Tetris actions to intuitive swipe and tap gestures.

1. **Mobile Touch Control Integration:** The `CoopInputHandler` is updated to process touch events (`touchstart`, `touchmove`, `touchend`).
2. **Gesture Mapping:** Standard Tetris actions are mapped to mobile gestures:
    * **Swipe Left/Right:** Move piece horizontally.
    * **Swipe Down:** Hard Drop.
    * **Swipe Up:** Hold piece.
    * **Tap:** Rotate piece.
    * **Long Press:** Soft Drop (continuous downward movement).

author: ratioactivity
body:
### Motivation
- Stored bookmarks were being overwritten or not loaded, leaving the UI empty and menus unresponsive on startup. 
- The restore flow still needs a way to explicitly re-apply default `bookmarks.json` without doing it on every launch. 
- Desktop/menu load handler registration and a recent edit introduced an initialization/syntax fragility that could prevent event handlers from attaching. 
- The Image Fridge grid can throw if its API isn't ready, causing further init disruptions.

### Description
- Change `hydrateData` to `hydrateData(options = {})` and add a `forceDefaults` flag so stored bookmarks are preserved by default; when `forceDefaults` is `true` the defaults from `DEFAULT_SOURCE` are fetched and applied. 
- Update the restore button handler to call `hydrateData({ forceDefaults: true })` so restores intentionally replace current bookmarks. 
- Move the bookmark hydration call into its own `window.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", ...)` invocation with `.catch()` logging to ensure it runs even if other init code throws. 
- Fix desktop/menu initialization by wrapping the desktop `load` handler registration in a proper `DOMContentLoaded` block (and restore the correct block closure), and guard Image Fridge refresh to use `window.BubblemarksImageFridge.loadImages()` only when the API is available.

### Testing
- Ran a syntax check with `node --check script.js`, which completed successfully. 
- No unit tests were added or run beyond the syntax check. 
- Verified script builds and commits were created for each logical fix via incremental commits. 
- No changes were made to any data files (per project constraints).

author: copilot
body:
The `WithSentiment()`, `WithProductArea()`, and `WithRegion()` methods in `FeedbackQueryBuilder` directly interpolated user input into SQL strings, enabling SQL injection attacks.

## Changes

- **QueryBuilder**: Added `params []any` field and `WhereParam()` method for parameterized conditions using PostgreSQL placeholders ($1, $2, etc.)
- **FeedbackQueryBuilder**: Updated vulnerable methods to use `WhereParam()` instead of `fmt.Sprintf()` string interpolation
- **Repository interface**: Modified `QueryFeedback()` to accept variadic parameters: `QueryFeedback(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any)`
- **API**: Added `BuildWithParams()` method returning both query string and parameters; existing `Build()` maintained for backward compatibility
- **Tests**: Added SQL injection prevention tests and parameterization validation

## Example

**Before (vulnerable):**
```go
fqb.Where(fmt.Sprintf("sentiment = '%s'", sentiment))  // SQL injection risk
```

**After (secure):**
```go
fqb.WhereParam("sentiment = %s", sentiment)  // Uses $1 placeholder
query, params := fqb.BuildFeedbackWithParams()  // Returns: "...WHERE sentiment = $1", ["negative"]
```

Documentation updated to reflect parameterized query usage patterns.

author: jasongross
body:
This PR allows challenges that demand the construction of terms of
non-Prop types.

We remove the error "Challenge and solution constant kind don't match"
in favor of permitting any kind of solution to a challenge that is a
theorem or axiom.

Note that permitted axioms must still be declared as axioms or theorems
in the solution; it would invite inconsistency if we allowed
instantiating informative axioms with definitions.

The optional field "allow_partial" indicates whether or not challenges
may be solved with `partial def` solutions.  We uniformly forbid unsafe
solutions.  We rely on the Lean kernel to mark as unsafe (resp. partial)
any definitions that make use of unsafe (resp. partial) dependencies.


This is a more invasive and global change than #7, but I believe it is more principled and better designed.  (And when you exclude the 21 loc in Comparator/Utils.lean which is present only for having nicer error messages, it is actually a net reduction of -10 loc.)

Axioms is now responsible for ensuring that solutions to challenges are present and have valid kinds (no forbidden axioms recursively; only partial if permitted; not unsafe)

Compare is is responsible for ensuring that:
- targets are present and are axioms or theorems in the challenge file
- targets have the same type in the challenge and solution
- any dependency of a solution, which is not an explicit target, and which occurs in both the challenge and the solution, has the same contents in both

Fixes #3 (mostly)
Fixes #4
Closes #5
Closes #6
Closes #7

author: copilot
body:
Built a React Native + Expo app enabling Sierra Club donating members to discover hiking and biking trails. Single codebase deploys to Web, iOS, and Android.

## Implementation

**Member Verification**
- Code-based auth: 6-character alphanumeric codes (email delivery)
- Admin portal: Direct verification via @sierraclub.org credentials
- Persistent sessions using AsyncStorage

**Trail Discovery**
- 8 sample trails with distance, elevation, difficulty, features, ratings
- Filter by activity type (hiking/biking/all)
- GPS-based proximity sorting
- Location permission handling with graceful degradation

**Architecture**
- React Navigation stack: Verification → Home → Trail List → Trail Detail
- Context API for auth state management
- Expo Location for geolocation
- React Native Web for browser compatibility

## Technical Approach

Authentication flow with demo validation:
```javascript
// Member code: any 6-char alphanumeric
const validCodePattern = /^[A-Za-z0-9]{6}$/;

// Admin: @sierraclub.org domain + 8+ chars
if (email.includes('@sierraclub.org') && password.length >= MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
  // Grant access
}
```

Trail sorting by user location:
```javascript
export const sortTrailsByDistance = (trails, userLat, userLon) => {
  return trails
    .map(trail => ({
      ...trail,
      distanceFromUser: calculateDistance(userLat, userLon, trail.latitude, trail.longitude),
    }))
    .sort((a, b) => a.distanceFromUser - b.distanceFromUser);
};
```

## Screenshots

**Member Verification**
![Verification](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77e9ab47-0b97-4a4d-83d9-ea379874381c)

**Home Dashboard**
![Home](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1579fa2-3def-485d-a19d-95ea1bcd9222)

**Trail List**
![List](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89df5978-01a1-404d-a626-263c275d7d86)

**Trail Details**
![Detail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7c20cfb-d607-488d-944f-1c22d0b63584)

## Production Readiness

Current: Client-side validation with sample data for demo
Required: Backend API for code generation/verification, trail database, JWT tokens, HTTPS

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for API design and security requirements.

## Running

```bash
npm install
npm run web      # Browser at localhost:8081
npm run ios      # Requires Xcode
npm run android  # Requires Android Studio
```

Demo: Any 6-char code (e.g., `TRAIL1`) or `admin@sierraclub.org` + 8+ char password

author: jackgww
body:
## Overview

Major refactoring of the LiveMap component to improve maintainability and user experience. Introduces a new bottom sheet pattern for recording history, modular map components, and custom React hooks for state management.

## Why

The LiveMap component had grown too large (~1100 lines) and mixed concerns. Recording history was displayed in a separate modal which felt disconnected from the map experience. This refactor:
- Improves code organization and maintainability
- Creates a more intuitive UX with the bottom sheet pattern
- Enables overlay functionality to compare past recordings with current route
- Makes the codebase easier to extend for future features

## Changes

### New Components (`src/components/map/`)
- **RecordingControls.js** - Record/pause/resume/save button cluster
- **StatsBar.js** - Distance, elevation, and time display during recording
- **MapControlButtons.js** - Location tracking and legend toggle buttons
- **OverlayPill.js** - Indicator pill when viewing a past recording overlay
- **Legend.js** - Trail difficulty legend overlay
- **RecordedRouteLayers.js** - Map layers for current, overlay, and history routes
- **ToastConfig.js** - Unified toast notification styling

### New Recording UI
- **HistoryBottomSheet.js** - Replaces RecordingDetailModal and RecordingHistoryScreen with a unified bottom sheet that animates smoothly between list and detail views
- Recording controls now use bottom navigation pattern for better discoverability

### Custom Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- **useRecording.js** - Manages recording state, GPS filtering, and stats calculation
- **useHistorySheet.js** - Controls history bottom sheet view state
- **useOverlay.js** - Manages past recording overlay display with animations
- **useLocationMode.js** - Handles location tracking mode cycling

### Trail Marker Updates
- Switched to Mapbox symbol-based markers for better performance
- Generated `all_markers.json` for consolidated marker data

### Code Cleanup
- LiveMap reduced from ~1100 to ~660 lines
- Removed deprecated files: CustomMarker.js, RecordingDetailModal.js, RecordingHistoryScreen.js
- Added shared constants for state enums (RecordingState, HistoryViewMode, LocationMode)
- New utility files: formatters.js, constants.js, mapConfig.js

The frontend at `https://akamoney-admin.pages.dev` was blocked by CORS policy because the backend only allowed `https://aka.money` and `https://www.aka.money`.

## Changes

- Added `https://akamoney-admin.pages.dev` to `allowedOrigins` in CORS middleware
- Added test coverage for the new origin

```typescript
const allowedOrigins = [
  'https://aka.money',
  'https://www.aka.money',
  'https://akamoney-admin.pages.dev',  // Added
  'http://localhost:5173',
  'http://localhost:8787'
];
```

This enables the admin frontend to make authenticated API requests to the backend without CORS errors.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> The frontend deployed at `https://akamoney-admin.pages.dev` is being blocked by CORS policy when making API requests to the backend:
> 
> ```
> Access to XMLHttpRequest at 'https://akamoney-admin-api.akamoney.workers.dev/api/urls?page=1&limit=20' 
> from origin 'https://akamoney-admin.pages.dev' has been blocked by CORS policy: 
> Response to preflight request doesn't pass access control check: 
> The 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header has a value 'https://aka.money' that is not equal to the supplied origin.
> ```
> 
> ## Root Cause
> 
> In `src/backend/src/middleware/cors.ts`, the `allowedOrigins` array does not include the Cloudflare Pages deployment URL:
> 
> ```typescript
> const allowedOrigins = [
>   'https://aka.money',
>   'https://www.aka.money',
>   'http://localhost:5173',
>   'http://localhost:8787'
> ];
> ```
> 
> ## Solution Required
> 
> Add `https://akamoney-admin.pages.dev` to the `allowedOrigins` array in `src/backend/src/middleware/cors.ts`:
> 
> ```typescript
> const allowedOrigins = [
>   'https://aka.money',
>   'https://www.aka.money',
>   'https://akamoney-admin.pages.dev',  // Add this line
>   'http://localhost:5173',
>   'http://localhost:8787'
> ];
> ```
> 
> ## Expected Outcome
> 
> After this change:
> - The frontend at `https://akamoney-admin.pages.dev` will be able to make API requests to the backend
> - CORS preflight requests will succeed
> - Users can successfully load their URLs and analytics data
> 
> ## Files to Modify
> 
> - `src/backend/src/middleware/cors.ts`
> 


</details>

body: ## Description The CI was failing due to an update in `google.golang.org/api` (v0.258.0) which introduced stricter handling of credential options. The GCS retriever test was failing with `dialing: multiple credential options provided` because it was providing both `option.WithCredentials` and `option.WithHTTPClient`. This PR resolves the issue by: - Replacing `option.WithCredentials(&google.Credentials{})` with `option.WithoutAuthentication()` when using a mock HTTP client in the GCS retriever test. - Removing an unused `golang.org/x/oauth2/google` import. To test the change, run `go test ./retriever/gcstorageretriever/...`. ## Closes issue(s) Resolve # ## Checklist - [ ] I have tested this code - [ ] I have added unit test to cover this code - [ ] I have updated the documentation (`README.md` and `/website/docs`) - [ ] I have followed the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) ---

author: copilot
body:
Diff preview requests from concurrent Neovim instances were being routed to any running instance. Routine operations generated excessive notifications.

## Multi-session isolation

- **Session scoping**: Each Neovim instance generates unique ID (`nvim-{pid}-{timestamp}-{random}`) for isolated communication directories and MCP server registration
- **Communication paths**: `~/.local/share/claucode/diffs/<session-id>/` ensures diffs route to correct instance
- **MCP server names**: Auto-generate `claucode-nvim-<session-id>` (configurable via `mcp.server_name` for shared configs)
- **Cleanup**: VimLeavePre removes session-specific MCP servers and stops watchers

## Notification system

- **Helper module** (`notify.lua`): Centralized notification management with config caching
- **Selective silence**: `notifications.silent_watcher` and `notifications.silent_claude_md` default to true; errors/warnings always visible
- **Configurable icons**: `ui.icons.enabled` controls emoji display (❌ ⚠️ ℹ️ 🤔 💭 etc.)

## UX improvements

- **`:Claude` prompting**: No args opens `vim.ui.input` instead of showing usage error
- **TypeScript MCP server**: Accepts session ID as `process.argv[2]` for scoped communication

**Configuration:**

```lua
require("claucode").setup({
  mcp = {
    server_name = nil, -- Auto-generated; set custom name to share across sessions
  },
  ui = {
    icons = { enabled = true },
  },
  notifications = {
    silent_watcher = true,
    silent_claude_md = true,
  },
})
```

**Multi-instance behavior:**

```vim
" Instance 1: ~/.local/share/claucode/diffs/nvim-12345-1234567890-5678/
" Instance 2: ~/.local/share/claucode/diffs/nvim-67890-1234567891-9012/
" Diffs isolated, MCP servers independent
```

Backwards compatible. Existing configs work unchanged.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Create a PR for avifenesh/claucode.nvim focused on end-user UX and multi-session diff correctness:
> 
> 1) Multi-session diff correctness:
> - Introduce a unique per-Neovim-session identifier.
> - Ensure diff preview requests are routed only to the correct Neovim instance by scoping the communication directory and/or request filenames to the session id.
> - Ensure MCP server registration name can be unique per session (configurable), to prevent collisions across concurrent Neovim sessions and projects.
> - Update mcp_manager.lua to add/remove the session-specific MCP server name and to store/compute the active name consistently.
> - Update documentation (README and/or doc/mcp-diff-preview.md) to explain multi-session behavior and configuration.
> 
> 2) UX:
> - Add configurable UI icons/emojis (allow disabling); default to current behavior.
> - Add a small notification helper and reduce noisy notifications by default (especially watcher start/stop and CLAUDE.md updates), while keeping warnings/errors visible.
> - Make :Claude with no args open vim.ui.input prompt.
> 
> Constraints:
> - Keep backwards compatibility where possible; provide sane defaults.
> - Ensure timers/watchers are cleaned up on VimLeavePre.
> - Add minimal tests or self-checks if feasible.
> 
> Repository: avifenesh/claucode.nvim
> Base branch: main


</details>

author: wrightmat
body:
### Motivation
- Make the inspector more compact by keeping font-size/angle/curve inputs inline with their labels and keeping all text-orientation radios on a single row.  
- Treat `Curve` as `0` by default for non-curved orientations and apply the curved default only when a curved orientation is selected.  
- Ensure curved text hugs the chip edge (overlaps the image if needed) and aligns top/bottom bounds with horizontal text.  
- Preserve readable font sizing so curved text appears comparable to non-curved orientations.

### Description
- Updated `undercroft/press/index.html` to shorten the `Binding / Text` textarea, render the custom font-size input inline, add a nowrap orientation radio group, and place `Angle` + `Curve` (renamed) on a single inline row.  
- Added compact layout and curved-text helpers to `undercroft/press/css/styles.css` (`template-radio-group--nowrap`, `.press-text-orientation-group`, `.press-inline-input`, `.press-text-transform-row`, and `.press-curved-text--up/--down`) to prevent wrapping and control curved-SVG positioning.  
- Changed `undercroft/press/js/app.js` so `resolveTextTransform` computes a `defaultCurve` of `0` for non-curved orientations and `12` for curved ones and updated inspector initialization and orientation-change handlers to set `textCurve` and the UI value to `0` or `12` as appropriate.  
- Refined `undercroft/press/js/template-renderer.js` to size the curved-text SVG by the computed `fontSize`, apply a slight curved-font scale, increase curve responsiveness (`rawCurve * 1.6` capped), tighten arc endpoints, and add directional wrapper classes so curved-up/down placement anchors to the same top/bottom bounds as horizontal text while allowing overlap.

### Testing
- Started a local dev server with `python -m http.server` to serve the Press UI and the server responded successfully.  
- Fetched `press/index.html` via `curl` to confirm the page is served (succeeded).  
- Ran Playwright scripts to load `press/index.html` and capture screenshots; initial runs timed out waiting for some dynamic selectors, but a subsequent run produced a screenshot artifact (partial success).  
- All changes are UI/layout-only; no unit tests were added.

author: handover2ai-byexistence
body:
### Summary
This PR introduces flexible Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) device filtering to the Export-IntuneManagedDevices script.

### What’s New
- Added `-AVDDevices` switch to enable filtering for both AVD single-session and multi-session hosts.
- Added `-AVDUniqueIdentifier` parameter to support tenant-specific naming conventions.
- Default behavior filters AVD devices using `model = "Virtual Machine"`.
- When `-AVDUniqueIdentifier` is provided, the script filters devices by matching the identifier within `deviceName`.

### Why This Matters
Intune does not consistently expose `operatingSystemEdition` for AVD hosts, making OS-based filtering unreliable.  
This update provides a predictable and tenant-agnostic way to target AVD devices while still allowing precise overrides when naming conventions are available.

### Backward Compatibility
- No changes to default behavior unless `-AVDDevices` is explicitly used.
- Existing exports and authentication flows remain unchanged.

### Testing
- Verified filtering using both default model-based logic and custom name identifiers.
- Confirmed correct device counts and expected output in JSON and CSV exports.

author: hanfa
body:
This PR adds OpenTelemetry tracing support to the vLLM production stack router, enabling end-to-end distributed tracing across the inference pipeline. When enabled via `--otel-endpoint` (or Helm's `routerSpec.otel.endpoint`), the router extracts incoming W3C Trace Context headers (`traceparent, tracestate`), creates spans for routing operations, and propagates trace context to backend vLLM engines. This allows operators to visualize the complete request flow from client through router to engine in observability platforms like Jaeger. The implementation includes a new `experimental/otel` module with helper functions for span management, CLI arguments for configuration, Helm chart integration with schema validation, unit tests for both Python and Helm templates, and updated documentation in the distributed tracing tutorial. Tracing auto-enables when an OTLP endpoint is provided, requiring no additional feature flags. An example command of launching vLLM Router with Otel enabled: ``` vllm-router --port 8001 --service-discovery static --static-backends "http://localhost:8000" \ --static-models "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct" --routing-logic roundrobin \ --otel-endpoint localhost:4317 ``` FIX #773 **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ THE CHECKLIST BELOW AND FILL IN THE DESCRIPTION ABOVE** --- - [x] Make sure the code changes pass the [pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/production-stack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) checks. - [x] Sign-off your commit by using -s when doing git commit - [x] Try to classify PRs for easy understanding of the type of changes, such as `[Bugfix]`, `[Feat]`, and `[CI]`. ### Testing I use my local machine for testing with following setup (Semantic Router + Production Stack integration) ``` Envoy (8080) ↓ Semantic Router (50051 gRPC / 8080 HTTP) ↓ vLLM Production Stack Router (8001) ← NEW ↓ vLLM Engine (8000) ``` Without the vLLM Router enabling the Otel (you need this change of Semantic Router side https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/pull/852): With vLLM Router enabling the Otel: Note: Right now only the following endpoints have this tracing gap filled | Endpoint | Description | |----------------------|----------------------| | /v1/chat/completions | Chat completions API | | /v1/completions | Text completions API | | /v1/embeddings | Embeddings API | | /tokenize | Tokenization | | /detokenize | Detokenization | | /v1/rerank | Reranking API (v1) | | /rerank | Reranking API | | /v1/score | Scoring API (v1) | | /score | Scoring API | | /v1/responses | Responses API | Endpoints without tracing: - `/v1/audio/transcriptions` - uses `route_transcription_request()` - Disaggregated prefill requests - uses `route_disaggregated_prefill_request()` - Health/metrics endpoints (`/health`, `/v1/models`, etc.)

### Motivation

- Provide a modern, Access-inspired Windows desktop application to create and manage Access-compatible `.accdb` databases with a polished UI.  
- Store UI/workspace metadata alongside databases without shipping database binaries by using a sidecar `.badb.json` file.  
- Target Visual Studio/.NET Windows Forms to deliver a familiar object-explorer + designer workflow for tables, queries, forms, and reports.  
- Support creating `.accdb` files and tables programmatically using ADOX/OleDb when the Access Database Engine is available.

### Description

- Add a Visual Studio solution `BrokenArrowDbms.sln` and a WinForms project `src/BrokenArrowDbms` with `Program.cs` and `app.manifest`.  
- Implement a rich `MainForm` UI with menus, toolbar, object explorer, workspace tabs, a welcome tab, and handlers to create/open/save projects.  
- Add models `DatabaseProject`, `DatabaseObject`, and `DatabaseObjectType`, plus `InputDialog` in `Views` for simple input prompts.  
- Add services: `ProjectStore` for JSON sidecar persistence (`.badb.json`) and `AccessDatabaseService` to create `.accdb` files via `ADOX.Catalog` and tables via `System.Data.OleDb`.

### Testing

- Attempted `dotnet build` was not run because the environment lacks the .NET SDK, so no build verification was performed.  
- There are no automated unit tests included in this change set, so no automated test suite was executed.

author: antisgoat
body:
### Motivation

- Safari was failing uploads with a CORS preflight 404 to `firebasestorage.googleapis.com` when the browser constructed `/v0/b/.../o?name=` requests.
- Investigation showed the Firebase Storage SDK upload path (`uploadBytesResumable` in `uploadPreparedPhoto.ts`) was being driven to an incorrect host when runtime `storageBucket` values were non-canonical (e.g., a `*.firebasestorage.app` host or a full URL).
- The goal is to ensure uploads use the Firebase Web SDK (no manual REST POSTs) and retain the existing stall/watchdog behavior so iOS Safari does not hang or loop.

### Description

- Normalize `storageBucket` at initialization in `src/lib/firebase.ts` so values like `gs://...`, `https://.../v0/b/...`, or `*.firebasestorage.app` are converted to the canonical `...appspot.com` bucket name before calling `initializeApp`.
- Switch debug Storage Write Test to use the SDK resumable upload (`uploadBytesResumable`) and expose the resolved `app.options.storageBucket` value in the `?debug=1` scan debug panels by importing `getFirebaseApp` in `src/pages/Scan.tsx` and `src/pages/Scan/Result.tsx`.
- Files changed: `src/lib/firebase.ts`, `src/pages/Scan.tsx`, `src/pages/Scan/Result.tsx`.
- The existing resumable uploader and stall/paused watchdog in `src/lib/uploads/uploadPreparedPhoto.ts` remain in place and continue to use `uploadBytesResumable` for real uploads.

### Testing

- Ran `npm run lint`, which surfaced existing repo warnings/errors and did not fully pass in this environment (repo has preexisting lint issues). 
- Ran `npm run build`, which succeeded and produced a production build without errors. 
- Manual device verification steps (to run on an iPhone Safari): open the app with `?debug=1`, confirm `storageBucketApp` and `storageBucketResolved` are `mybodyscan-f3daf.appspot.com`, run the debug Storage Write Test and then perform a full scan upload front→back→left→right expecting no CORS/preflight 404s and successful completions.

author: severity1
body:
## Summary

Add `DebugWriter io.Writer` field to Options for custom debug output redirection, achieving Python SDK `debug_stderr` parity using Go's idiomatic `io.Writer` interface.

## Changes

### Files Modified
- `internal/shared/options.go` - Add `DebugWriter io.Writer` field to Options struct
- `options.go` - Add functional options (`WithDebugWriter`, `WithDebugStderr`, `WithDebugDisabled`)
- `options_test.go` - Add comprehensive table-driven tests
- `internal/subprocess/transport.go` - Use custom DebugWriter when set, fall back to temp file

### API Additions
```go
// Custom writer for capturing debug output
var debugBuf bytes.Buffer
client := NewClient(WithDebugWriter(&debugBuf))

// Convenience: redirect to stderr
client := NewClient(WithDebugStderr())

// Convenience: discard all debug output
client := NewClient(WithDebugDisabled())

// Default (nil): temp file isolation for deadlock prevention
client := NewClient() // No debug writer - same as before
```

## Test Plan
- [x] All tests passing with `go test -race -cover ./...`
- [x] Coverage maintained at 86.4% (main package)
- [x] Race detector clean
- [x] `go fmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` all pass
- [x] Python SDK parity verified for `debug_stderr` functionality

## Design Decisions

1. **`io.Writer` interface** - Go-native, composable, works with all logging libraries
2. **Default nil** - Maintains current temp file isolation behavior for deadlock prevention
3. **`json:"-"` tag** - Not serializable, runtime-only configuration
4. **No `WithDebugFile()`** - YAGNI; users can create file writers themselves
5. **Convenience functions** - `WithDebugStderr()` and `WithDebugDisabled()` for common use cases

Closes #12

## Summary

Upgrade GitHub Actions to their latest versions to ensure compatibility with Node 24, as Node 20 will reach end-of-life in April 2026.

## Changes

| Action | Old Version(s) | New Version | Release | Files |
|--------|---------------|-------------|---------|-------|
| `actions/checkout` | [`v4`](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v4) | [`v6`](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v6) | [Release](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v6) | ci.yml, git-xet-release.yml, hf-xet-tests.yml, pre-release-testing.yml, release.yml |
| `actions/download-artifact` | [`v4`](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v4), [`v5`](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v5) | [`v7`](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v7) | [Release](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v7) | git-xet-release.yml, release.yml |
| `actions/setup-python` | [`v5`](https://github.com/actions/setup-python/releases/tag/v5) | [`v6`](https://github.com/actions/setup-python/releases/tag/v6) | [Release](https://github.com/actions/setup-python/releases/tag/v6) | hf-xet-tests.yml, release.yml |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | [`v4`](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v4) | [`v6`](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v6) | [Release](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v6) | git-xet-release.yml, release.yml |

## Context

Per [GitHub's announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/), Node 20 is being deprecated and runners will begin using Node 24 by default starting March 4th, 2026.

### Why this matters

- **Node 20 EOL**: April 2026
- **Node 24 default**: March 4th, 2026
- **Action**: Update to latest action versions that support Node 24

### Security Note

Actions that were previously pinned to commit SHAs remain pinned to SHAs (updated to the latest release SHA) to maintain the security benefits of immutable references.

### Testing

These changes only affect CI/CD workflow configurations and should not impact application functionality. The workflows should be tested by running them on a branch before merging.

Creates a minimal Express.js application with MongoDB support for deployment on Render.

## Implementation

- **package.json**: Node.js 18+ project with `npm install` build and `npm start` commands
- **server.js**: Express server with Mongoose MongoDB connection, `/` and `/health` endpoints, CORS enabled
- **.env.example**: Environment variable template for `MONGO_URI` configuration
- **.gitignore**: Excludes node_modules and build artifacts
- **README.md**: Two-step deployment instructions and local development setup

## Configuration

Render deployment requires:
- Build Command: `npm install`
- Start Command: `npm start`  
- Environment Variable: `MONGO_URI` (MongoDB connection string)

Server gracefully handles missing MongoDB connection, allowing deployment before database provisioning.

```javascript
// MongoDB connection with fallback
mongoose.connect(MONGO_URI)
  .then(() => console.log('MongoDB connected successfully'))
  .catch((err) => {
    console.error('MongoDB connection error:', err);
    // App continues without DB
  });
```
